rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognized his brothers immediately through keen perception: their former and present appearances remained alike, and they were now mature men.
rows.anchor: فعرفهم في بادىء الرأي وأول النظر لقوة فهمه وعدم مباينة أحوالهم السابقة لحالهم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had been intent on learning their condition during the famine and expected them because God had promised he would tell them of their deed at the well.
rows.anchor: ولكون همته معقودة بهم وبمعرفة أحوالهم لا سيما في زمان القحط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says forty years passed between the brothers throwing Joseph into the well and their arriving before him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إنه كان بين أن قذفوه في البئر وبين أن دخلوا عليه أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They failed to recognize Joseph because of the long separation, his youth when they last saw him, their belief he had died, and the gulf between the helpless boy and the ruler.
rows.anchor: وهم له منكرون أي والحال إنهم منكرون ليوسف لطول العهد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says Joseph recognized them by prophetic gnosis, while their sins and lack of repentance veiled them from recognizing him; true recognition would have kept them from selling him cheaply.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية عرفهم بنور المعرفة والنبوة وهم له منكرون لبقاء ظلمة معاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph supplied their travel provisions and loaded their mounts; he said “a brother of yours from your father” rather than “your brother” to signal that he did not know them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بأخيكم مبالغة في إظهار عدم معرفته لهم فإنه فرق بين مررت بغلامك ومررت بغلام لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers may have requested an extra ration for Benjamin; Joseph granted it on condition that they bring him, while normally giving one load per person to distribute grain fairly.
rows.anchor: سألوه حملا زائدا على المعتاد لبنيامين فأعطاهم ذلك وشرطهم أن يأتوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary distinguishes paternal half-brothers, full siblings, and maternal half-siblings in explaining the family wording.
rows.anchor: والعلة الضرة وبنوا العلات بنوا أمهات شتى من رجل

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the brothers asked for another camel-load for Benjamin; Joseph replied that he rationed by the number of people, not by the number of camels.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (هريك را يك شتر بار كندم دادن كفتنديك شتروار ديكر بجهت برادر

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlūm reports that Joseph questioned the brothers in Hebrew, suspected they might be spies, and heard that they were famine-struck shepherds and sons of Jacob.
rows.anchor: وقال في بحر العلوم لا بد من مقدمة سبقت له معهم حتى اجترأ القول هذه المسألة

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: In the report, Joseph demanded a hostage, Benjamin, and a letter from Jacob; a lot selected Simeon to remain behind.
rows.anchor: فدعوا بعضكم عندي رهينة وائتوني بأخيكم من أبيكم وهو يحمل رسالة من أبيكم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Joseph assured them he would give the full measure and was the best of hosts; he spoke to urge them to do what he required, not to boast.
rows.anchor: لم يقله عليه السلام بطريق الامتنان بل لحثهم على تحقيق ما أمرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they failed to bring Benjamin, Joseph would withhold future grain and bar them from approaching his land, let alone receiving his hospitality.
rows.anchor: فلا كيل لكم عندي من بعد ، أي في المستقبل فضلا عن إيفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may be either a prohibition or a negation coordinated with the conditional consequence; on either reading it falls under the penalty.
rows.anchor: وهو إما نهي أو نفي معطوف على الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says Joseph was commanded to seek Benjamin so Jacob's reward for separation would be increased.
rows.anchor: قالوا : الله أمره بطلب أخيه ليعظم أجر أبيه على فراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their earlier conduct, Jacob would not send Benjamin until they gave a solemn, oath-confirmed covenant invoking God; the pledge is permitted because God authorizes oaths by Him.
rows.anchor: موثقا من الله أي عهدا موثوقا به أي معتمدا مؤكدا بالحلف وذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “unless you are surrounded” means either being overpowered so they cannot bring Benjamin or all being killed.
rows.anchor: إلا وقت الإحاطة بكم وكونهم محاطا بهم إما كناية عن كونهم مغلوبين مقهورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's words fulfill the proverb that a calamity is tied to speech: his earlier fear of a wolf was echoed in the brothers' false claim, and now he is truly surrounded.
rows.anchor: ولقد صدقت هذه القصة المثل السائر وهو قولهم البلاء موكل بالمنطق

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reports that the brothers swore by the right of Muhammad, seal of the prophets, not to betray Benjamin.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (درتبيان فرموده كه اورا بشما ندهم تا سوكند خوريد بحق محمد خاتم النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God a witness after the pledge expresses reliance on Him and urges both sides to honor their covenant.
rows.anchor: قال الله على ما نقول وكيل أي على ما قلنا في أثناء طلب الموثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance follows taking a firm decision; al-Kawāshī also treats this verse as evidence that outward means are compatible with sound trust in God.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن التوكل بعد التوكيد

rows.speaker: المثنوى
rows.claim: The cited couplet counsels that a person who relies on God should still do the work.
rows.anchor: كر توكل ميكنى در كار كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment belongs exclusively to God, so Jacob entrusts all his actions and abstentions to Him; the command to trust follows because prophetic conduct gives others an example.
rows.anchor: أحد سواه بشيء من السوء وغيره عليه لا على أحد سواه توكلت

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustarī says God determines servants' obligations, lifespans, and provision, while servants must trust God, follow His Prophet, and remain patient until death.
rows.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري قدس سره للعباد على الله ثلاثة أشياء تكليفهم وآجالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first three matters do not arise through human effort and nothing is incumbent on God; the latter three require the servant to act.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ذلك أن الثلاثة الأول دخول العبد فيها تكلف إذ لا يتصور وجودها بسبب منه

rows.speaker: الكمال الجندي
rows.claim: Al-Kamāl al-Jundī's Persian verse invokes the evil eye as a real harm despite reason's tendency to dismiss it.
rows.anchor:
قال الكمال الجندي :
عقل باطل شمرد شم توهر خون كه كند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil eye is affirmed by scholars' experience and the convergent testimony of prophets; a hadith says it can put a person in the grave and a camel in the cooking pot.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه قد شهدت بإصابة العين تجاريب العلماء من الزمن الأقدم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports Gabriel told the Prophet that al-Hasan and al-Husayn had been struck by the evil eye and that the evil eye is real.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه إن جبريل أتى النبي فوافقه مغتما فقال يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Sunni doctrine, the eye has no intrinsic causal power; the resulting harm is God's customary act, while some thinkers allow the soul to affect other bodies through psychic influence.
rows.anchor: إذ لا تأثير للعين حقيقة على ما هو مذهب أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's sons entered by separate gates, with the phrase functioning as a circumstantial description of their entering apart.
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال ، أي دخلوا متفرقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither Jacob's plan nor their compliance could avert what God had decreed; the only benefit was to satisfy Jacob's concern and caution about the evil eye.
rows.anchor: ما كان يغني عنهم رأي يعقوب ودخولهم متفرقين من الله من جهته تعالى من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A need in Jacob” means, by exception in the sense of “but,” that he expressed and urged his compassionate precaution without believing planning could change decree.
rows.anchor: إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضيها حاجة منصوبة بإلا لكونها بمعنى لكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil eye did not strike them because it was not decreed; had it been decreed, they would have been struck together or apart, and Jacob knew this by revelation and proof.
rows.anchor: وأما إصابة العين فإنما لم تقع لكونها غير مقدرة عليهم لا لأنها اندفعت بذلك

rows.speaker: المثنوى
rows.claim: The cited verses say that all the world's schemes cannot defeat heaven's decree.
rows.anchor: كرشود ذرات عالم حيله ي باقضاى آسمان هيست هي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says outwardly focused people do not know that what happens to God's elect follows His revelation, inspiration, and teaching, while God acts as He wills.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية ولكن أرباب الصورة لا يعلمون أن ما يجري على خواص العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph welcomed and honored his brothers, then seated them two at a time at a dish.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم أحسنتم وستجدون ذلك عندي فاجلسوا فجلسوا على حاشية البساط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest brother hopes God will judge in his favor by a way that does not break the covenant or that frees Benjamin.
rows.anchor: أو يحكم الله لي بالخروج منها على وجه لا يؤدي إلى نقض الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best judge because He rules only with truth and justice; Kashifi says His judgment contains no partiality.
rows.anchor: وهو خير الحاكمين إذ لا يحكم إلا بالحق والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say they testify only to what they saw—the cup was taken from Benjamin's bag—and cannot attest to the hidden facts or whether he was framed.
rows.anchor: وما شهدنا عليه بالسرقة إلا بما علمنا وشاهدنا أن الصواع استخرج من وعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest advises them to ask the Egyptian town and the caravan they traveled with; the caravan were Canaanites from Jacob's neighborhood, and the inquiry is meant to clear their suspicion.
rows.anchor: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها أي : وقولوا لأبيكم أرسل إلى أهل مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest brother returned to Joseph and asked to be detained with Benjamin; Joseph kept them together and treated them well.
rows.anchor: قال إنك اتخذت أخي رهينة فخذني معه فجعله عند أخيه وأحسن إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob suspects that his sons had embellished the plan to accuse Benjamin, since the theft penalty was from Jacob's law and the Egyptian king would not have known it without their instruction.
rows.anchor: بل سولت لكم زينت وسهلت أنفسكم أمرا من الأمور اردتموه ففعلتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asks God to return Joseph, Benjamin, and the eldest son detained in Egypt; three sons are absent because the first loss left eleven and the second trip brought back nine.
rows.anchor: أي : بيوسف وأخيه والمتوقف بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob acknowledges God's complete knowledge of his grief and wisdom in trying him for a profound purpose.
rows.anchor: إنه هو العليم بحالي في الحزن والأسف الحكيم الذي لم يبتلني إلا لحكمة بالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trials are punishment, a test that reveals a person's inner state and rank, or an honor that raises closeness; patience and steadiness bring great reward in all three.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن البلاء على ثلاثة أضرب ، منها تعجيل عقوبة للعبد

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb reports that God told Jacob his separation from Joseph was punishment because he roasted a young animal, skimped on his neighbor, and ate without feeding him.
rows.anchor: كما قال وهب : أوحى الله إلى يعقوب أتدري لما عاقبتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts say Jacob's trial arose from slaughtering a calf before its mother, or selling a slave woman's child so she wept until blind, or refusing meat to a poor visitor.
rows.anchor: وروى أن سبب ابتلاء يعقوب إنه ذبح عجلا بين يدي أمه وهو يخور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job exemplifies a trial that reveals patience, while John son of Zechariah exemplifies honor through martyrdom despite having committed no sin; patience earns reward.
rows.anchor: وأما الامتحان فمثل ما نزل بأيوب عليه السلام قال تعالى : إنا وجدناه صابرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A worshipper who wept from the cold during his night prayer heard after a year that he had awakened people only to weep; he awoke and sought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقام بعضهم ليقضي ورده من الليل فأصابه البرد فبكى من شدته

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī quotes al-Daqqāq: divine support is shown by preserving oneness of God while decrees cut a person apart, yet the person remains still.
rows.anchor: قال أبو القاسم القشيري : سمعت الأستاذ أبا علي الدقاق ، يقول في آخر عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turned away because he could not bear what he heard; Kashifi says he retreated to the House of Sorrows, and Jami's verse pictures him asking to be left there alone.
rows.anchor: أعرض يعقوب عنهم كراهة لما سمع منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Yā asafā” names the most intense grief; it derives from “my grief,” with the final yā changed to alif for ease, and personifies grief as summoned to come.
rows.anchor: الأسف : أشد الحزن والحسرة ، وأصله يا أسفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob laments Joseph rather than his more recent losses because his grief for Joseph remained fresh, Joseph's loss was the source of his woes, and he expected the other two to return.
rows.anchor: وإنما تأسف على يوسف مع أن الحادث مصيبة أخويه بنيامين والمحتبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says only Muhammad's community was taught to say “We belong to God and return to Him” in calamity; the commentary contrasts this with Jacob's lament.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : لم تعط أمة من الأمم إنا الله وإنا إليه راجعون عند المصيبة

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة
rows.claim: Abū Maysara says that, if admitted to Paradise, he would reproach Joseph for not sending a letter or news to ease his father's grief.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ميسرة قال لو إن الله أدخلني الجنة لعاتبت يوسف بما فعل بأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is “restrained” because he is filled with grief and anger toward his sons but keeps it within his heart.
rows.anchor: فهو كظيم مملوء من الغيظ على أولاده ممسك له في قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar of “you will not cease” omits the negative particle because the sense is unambiguous; an affirmative reading would require an emphatic lām or nūn.
rows.anchor: قالوا تالله تفتؤا أي لا تفتأ ولا تزال وحذفت لا لعدم الالتباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward lesson is that lovers face people's blame: even the angels reproached Adam, and the true lover does not fear blame in God's cause.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه لا بد للمحب من ملامة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he confides his grievous distress and sorrow to God alone, rather than complaining to his sons or anyone else.
rows.anchor: قال إنما أشكو بثي البث أصعب الهم الذي لا يصبر عليه صاحبه فيبثه إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Distress” is the hardest grief that must be disclosed, while “sorrow” is broader; paired with the specific term, it covers the remaining lesser griefs.
rows.anchor: والحزن أعم من البث ، فإذا عطف على الخاص يراد به الأفراد الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction between beautiful patience and lament: complaining to the Creator is allowed, as with Job, while patience means not complaining to others or relying on them.
rows.anchor: قيل : ليس هذا إلا شكاية من النفس إلى خالقها وهو جائز ، ألا ترى أن أيوب عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows God's mercy and kindness, so he hopes God will show compassion and not disappoint him.
rows.anchor: وأعلم من الله من لطفه ورحمته ما لا تعلمون فأرجو أن يرحمني ويلطف بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading is that inspiration gave Jacob knowledge that Joseph was alive; another report says he saw the Angel of Death in a dream and was told Joseph lived.
rows.anchor: أو أعلم من الله بنوع من الإلهام ما لا تعلمون من حياة يوسف وروى أنه رأى ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report says Jacob knew from Joseph's dream that he would live until his family prostrated to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل علم من رؤيا يوسف أنه لا يموت حتى يخروا له سجدا

rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: Joseph asks Gabriel about Jacob; Gabriel says God granted Jacob beautiful patience and tested him with grief, estimating his sorrow as that of seventy bereaved women and his reward as a hundred martyrs.
rows.anchor: وروى أن يوسف قال لجبريل : أيها الروح الأمين هل لك علم بيعقوب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the account of Egypt's ruler stirred Jacob's hope that the ruler might be Joseph, prompting him to send his sons to investigate.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : لما أخبره ولده بسيرة الملك أحست نفسه فطمع وقال لعله يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tahassus” means searching for news through one's senses; the cited lexicons distinguish it from “tajassus,” which can mean investigating through another person.
rows.anchor: أي تعرفوا من خبرهما بحواسكم فإن التحسس طلب الشيء بالحاسة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh explains that Jacob's turning away was turning to God and ceasing complaint to his sons, not a refusal to speak gently with them about another matter.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : فإن قلت كيف خاطبهم بهذا اللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob sends them to seek Joseph and Benjamin; he does not name the eldest brother because that brother chose to remain in Egypt, so his absence was easy to remedy.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الثالث وهو الذي قال فلن أبرح الأرض واحتبس بمصر لأن غيبته اختيارية

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawāshī explains God's “relief” as the heart's rest from grief and the relief that comes from God.
rows.anchor: قال في الكواشي : أصله استراحة القلب من غمه ؛ والمعنى لا تقنطوا من راحة تأتيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “rawḥ” with ḍamma, meaning God's mercy that gives life to servants.
rows.anchor: وقرىء من روح الله بالضم أي من رحمته التي يحيى بها العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only unbelievers despair of God's relief; knowers do not despair in hardship or ease and remember that ease accompanies hardship.
rows.anchor: إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون لعدم علمهم بالله وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says a sinful person who hopes is nearer to God than a worshipper who despairs.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "الفاجر الراجي أقرب إلى الله من العابد القانط"

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb reports that God forgave a notorious sinner who, despite sinning, inwardly hated sin, preferred the company of the righteous, and prioritized a righteous person's need.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية وهب بن منبه قال : يا رب لو عفوت عني لفرح أنبياؤك وأولياؤك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not despair: God relieves distress in this life and the next; the story of a stranded man ends with a ship arriving after he had given up hope.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا يقنط من رحمة ربه فإنه تعالى

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading tells every Muslim to seek the heart as Joseph and the secret as Benjamin, never despair of God's presence, and understand seeking and finding God as matters of the heart.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" في الآية إشارة إلى أن الواجب على كل مسلم

rows.speaker: المثنوى
rows.claim: The Masnavi verses urge relentless seeking by every route and faculty, echoing Jacob's command to search for Joseph and Benjamin and not despair.
rows.anchor:
وفي المثنوى :
كر كران وكر شتابنده بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has Jacob send a letter tracing his family through Abraham and Isaac, recalling their trials, his grief and blindness over Joseph, and insisting his family neither steals nor raises thieves.
rows.anchor: روي أن يعقوب أمر بعض أولاده فكتب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من يعقوب إسرائيل الله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the letter Jacob says Benjamin is being called a thief despite their household's innocence and threatens a prayer whose effect would reach Joseph's seventh descendant if Benjamin is not returned.
rows.anchor: وإنا أهل بيت لا نسرق ولا نلد سارقا ، فإن رددته علي وإلا دعوت عليك دعوة تدرك السابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers describe their family as stricken by poverty, need, many dependents, and little food, and present merchandise of little value.
rows.anchor: مسنا أصابنا وأهلنا وهم من خلفوهم الضر الفقر والحاجة وكثرة العيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mazjāh” means rejected or pushed-away goods; the commentary offers Bedouin wool and clarified butter, pine nuts or pistachios, and clipped or debased coins as possible merchandise.
rows.anchor: أي مردودة مدفوعة يدفعها كل تاجر رغبة عنها واحتقارا لها من ازجيته إذا دفعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to complete the measure asks Joseph to give the full ration due to them.
rows.anchor: فأوف لنا الكيل فأتم لنا الكيل الذي هو حقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet frames the brothers as bringing need, weakness, and helplessness rather than valuable merchandise.
rows.anchor: نيستى وحاجت وعجز ونياز آورده ام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing his brothers' humility moved Joseph so strongly that he could not restrain himself from revealing who he was.
rows.anchor: قال لما رأى يوسف تمسكن إخوته رق لهم فلم يتمالك من أن عرفهم نفسه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reports that Joseph read Jacob's letter, began to cry, and then addressed his brothers.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي (آن نامه يعقوب بركوشه تخت نهادند يوسف نامه را بخواند كريه بروى غلبه كرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks whether they have repented of their treatment of him and Benjamin; they had separated Benjamin from Joseph, hurt and humiliated him.
rows.anchor: أي : هل تبتم عن ذلك بعد علمكم بقبحه فهو سؤال عن الملزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When you were ignorant” means either ignorant of the deed's ugliness or unaware of what would happen to Joseph; Joseph speaks compassionately to counsel repentance, not to reproach them.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان كلامه هذا شفقة عليهم وتنصحا لهم في الدين وتحريضا على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a reported reply to Jacob, Joseph says that the patriarchs endured trials and prevailed; Jacob recognizes it as a prophetic letter and wonders whether its author is Joseph.
rows.anchor: فاصبر كما صبروا والسلام ، فلما قرأ يعقوب الكتاب ، قال : والله ما هذا كتاب الملوك

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Joseph removed his veil and crown, allowing his brothers to recognize his appearance and features.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آنكه نقاب افكند وتاج ازسر بر داشت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' question “Are you Joseph?” is a confirmation: his beauty and perfection made the answer unmistakable.
rows.anchor: قالوا أئنك لانت يوسف استفهام تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By identifying Benjamin as his full brother, Joseph emphasizes that God favored both with release, reunion after separation, and comfort after loneliness.
rows.anchor: قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي من أبي وأمي ذكره مبالغة في تعريف نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa means guarding oneself from God's anger and punishment; patience includes enduring separation, imprisonment, difficult worship, and resisting desired sins.
rows.anchor: يتق أي يفعل التقوى في جميع أحواله أويق نفسه عما يوجب سخط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not waste the reward of the beneficent; the description points to one who combines piety and patience.
rows.anchor: فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين أي : أجرهم وإنما وضع المظهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing Joseph, the brothers approach the throne intending to fall at his feet; he descends and embraces them.
rows.anchor: ون برادران يوسف را بشناختند روى بتخت آورده خواستند كه دراى وى افتند يوسف ازتخت فروده آمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers admit God favored Joseph in beauty, perfection, status, and wealth, and say they knowingly committed sin.
rows.anchor: اختارك وفضلك علينا بالجمال والكمال والجاه والمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No reproach” derives from removing the fat covering the stomach; severe blame is like melting a noble person's body, and Ibn al-Shaykh likens it to tearing honor and face.
rows.anchor: وهو تفعيل من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي يغشى الكرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Today” may limit the absence of blame to that day, implying all other days too, or attach to God's forgiveness: Joseph waived his personal claim and their repentance leaves God to forgive.
rows.anchor: واليوم منصوب بالتثريب أي لا تثريب عليكم اليوم الذي هو مظنة التثريب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says the brothers' first wrongdoing ultimately became the means of Joseph's elevation and kingship, so he prays for their forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية أخبر بصنيعهم في البداية ولكنه كان سبب رفعة منزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garment will restore Jacob's sight, as confirmed by the statement that he regained his sight; “come to me” addresses the brothers and their father.
rows.anchor: فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا يصير بصيرا ، كقولك : جاء البناء محكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your whole family” can include wives, children, enslaved people, relatives, companions, or all of them together.
rows.anchor: بأهلكم أجمعين بنسائكم وذراريكم ومواليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Judah carried the garment to atone for bringing the bloody shirt; he went barefoot and bareheaded, carrying seven loaves, and traveled eighty farsakhs before finishing them.
rows.anchor: روي أن يهودا حمل القميص وقال أنا أحزنته ، بحمل القميص الملطخ بالدم إليه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Joseph gave Judah the garment and prepared travel provisions and supplies for his brothers.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يراهن بوي داد وأسباب راه جهت در ومتعلقان مهيا ساخنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When the caravan departed” means it left the town and passed beyond its buildings; Kashifi specifies that it emerged from built-up Egypt into open country.
rows.anchor: ولما فصلت العير يقال فصل من البلد فصولا إذا انفصل منه وجاوز حيطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Jacob smell Joseph's clinging scent from eighty farsakhs away as Judah approached; the cited Persian verse links the shirt's scent with Jacob's perception.
rows.anchor: إني لأجد ريح يوسف أوجده الله ، أي جعله واجدا ريح ما عبق أي لزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sufi contrast says the heedless ascetic cannot know another's spiritual state, while the lover senses secret traces and the breath of divine mercy in manifestations.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الزاهد ذاهل عما عنده كالحمار الغافل عما استصحبه من الكتب

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of spiritual meanings say God withheld news during the trial despite nearby places, then delivered a scent from far away when relief came: hardship and ease change with God's favor.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : إن الله أوصل إليه رائحة يوسف عند انقضاء المحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those present accuse Jacob of his old excess in loving and remembering Joseph because they think Joseph died; the inward lesson says people blame lovers for their fixation.
rows.anchor: أي الحاضرون عنده تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle “an” after “when” is extra, emphasizing that the messenger's arrival and the shirt's being cast occurred as if at one instant.
rows.anchor: فلما أن إن صلة أي زائدة لتأكيد الفعلين واتصالهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer of good news is Judah; “irtadda” means to return to a former state, so Jacob regained both sight and his earlier strength and joy.
rows.anchor: القيه على وجهه طرح البشير القميص على وجه يعقوب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading compares the shirt to the heart's lights of beauty: the spirit was initially clear, became blind through worldly attachment, and regained sight through an inspiration from the heart.
rows.anchor: قال في التأويلات النجمية : فلما أن جاء البشير من حضرة يوسف القلب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart and spirit exchange roles: first the heart needs the spirit for completion, then the perfected heart illuminates the spirit; the heart is a lamp and the spirit its oil.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن القلب في بدو الأمر كان محتاجا إلى الروح في الاستكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he had told his sons that God had taught him what they did not know, including Joseph's life and the coming relief; the messenger confirms Joseph is Egypt's king and a Muslim.
rows.anchor: ألم أقل لكم يا بني حين أرسلتكم إلى مصر وأمرتكم بالتجسس ونهيتكم عن اليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness, admitting deliberate sins against him, Joseph, and Benjamin and appealing to his compassion.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا خاطئين متعمدين للخطيئة والإثم مذنبين بما فعلنا بك وبيوسف وبنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A promise with “soon” from a great person signals solemn certainty, not doubt; the delay expresses dignity and avoidance of haste.
rows.anchor: سوف وعسى ولعل في وعد الأكابر والعظماء يدل على صدق الأمر وجده

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says Jacob meant he would ask Joseph to forgive them, since the wronged person's pardon is a condition for forgiveness, and so he delayed until meeting him.
rows.anchor: وعن شعبي قال : سوف استغفر لكم ربي قال اسأل يوسف إن عفا عنكم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: In the same report Jacob prays before dawn on Friday night, Joseph says amen and the brothers stand humbly behind them; God reveals that He has forgiven them, and Jacob continues praying for them weekly for over twenty years.
rows.anchor: فلما قدموا عليه في مصر قام إلى الصلاة في السحر ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The shaykh's analysis contrasts Joseph's immediate forgiveness, arising from gratitude for the blessings his brothers' crime led to, with Jacob's delayed prayer until a sincere divinely permitted intention arose.
rows.anchor: انبعث من غيب قلب يوسف النظر إلى ما نال إليه بسبب إخوته من النعماء والآلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sent extensive supplies, including two hundred mounts, and invited Jacob to bring his whole family to Egypt.
rows.anchor: روى إن يوسف وجه إلى أبيه جهازا كثيرا ومائتي راحلة وسأله أن يأتيه بأهله أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph and the Egyptian king welcomed Jacob with a vast army and the dignitaries and people of Egypt; the report gives either four thousand soldiers or three hundred thousand horsemen, with silver and gold decorations.
rows.anchor: فاستقبله يوسف والملك الريان في أربعة آلاف من الجند أو ثلاثمائة ألف فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel says the angels also came to rejoice at the reunion, after having grieved for Jacob during his long sorrow.
rows.anchor: فقال له جبريل : انظر إلى الهواء فإن الملائكة قد حضرت سرورا بحالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel identifies Joseph beneath a canopy; Jacob leaps down and hurries with Judah's support, and Gabriel tells Joseph to dismount and let his older, more worthy father greet first.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل : يا يوسف إن أباك يعقوب قد نزل لك فأنزل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some of the interpretation” can mean that Joseph received only part of the detailed interpretive knowledge, even if he had the capacity for mastery; it may also mark a kind of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن للتبعيض أيضا لأنه لم يؤت علم كل التأويل على التفصيل

rows.speaker: ابن الكمال
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kamāl explains the morphology of “aḥādīth” and says it means dreams and their interpretation as the events to which they lead; this noble science is not intrinsic to prophecy or sainthood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الكمال : الأحاديث مبنى على واحده المستعمل وهو الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Originator of the heavens and earth” means their Creator, bringing them from nonexistence into existence; Ibn Abbas learned “fāṭir” from an Arab's claim that he began digging a well.
rows.anchor: فاطر السموات والأرض أي : خالقهما وموجدهما من العدم إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses God as Joseph's master and caretaker, the one who manages his affairs in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (تويى يا رمن ومتولى كارمن) أي القائم بأمري في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should praise God before presenting a need; Joseph's prayer follows that order.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن من عرض له حاجة فأراد أن يدعو فعليه أن يقدم الثناء على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Let me die as a Muslim” asks for death while firmly in Islam, the completion of blessing, or can mean being taken to God in pure monotheism; one report says Joseph alone among prophets wished for death.
rows.anchor: توفني مسلما وهو طلب للوفاة على حال الإسلام لأنها تمام النعمة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reports that Joseph dreamed of an impending meeting, made a will, appointed Judah his heir, and prayed; the kingdom he received was a great part of Egypt, not the whole world.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي (يوسف دررا بخواب ديدكه ميكويد اي يوسف بغايت مشاق لقاي توام

rows.speaker: إفتاده
rows.claim: Shaykh Iftādah says Joseph had an aptitude for temporal rule, while the Prophet of prophets annihilated every deed and attribute of his dominion and received an incomparable direct manifestation of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بافتاده قدس سره : كان في وجود يوسف عليه السلام قابلية السلطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some of the interpretation” may denote partial possession of detailed interpretive knowledge or identify its kind; dreams are the events to which visions lead, and interpretation is not an inherent requirement of prophethood or sainthood.
rows.anchor: ومن للتبعيض أيضا لأنه لم يؤت علم كل التأويل على التفصيل

rows.speaker: ابن الكمال
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kamāl gives the morphology of “aḥādīth” and defines interpretation as explaining what dreams will become in the world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الكمال : الأحاديث مبنى على واحده المستعمل وهو الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Originator of the heavens and earth” means their Creator, bringing them from nonexistence into existence.
rows.anchor: فاطر السموات والأرض أي : خالقهما وموجدهما من العدم إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas learned the meaning of “fāṭir” when two Arabs disputed ownership of a well and one said that he had initiated its digging.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان معنى الفاطر غير ظاهر لي إلى أن تقدم رجلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Let me die as a Muslim” requests death in Islam, the completion of blessing, or can mean being taken to God as a pure monotheist.
rows.anchor: توفني مسلما وهو طلب للوفاة على حال الإسلام لأنها تمام النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Join me with the righteous” can mean Joseph's prophetic ancestors in Paradise or the broader company of the righteous in blessing and honor; prophets are called righteous because they gather every virtue.
rows.anchor: وألحقنى بالصالحين} أي بآبائي المرسلين في الجنة

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī objects that a great prophet should not ask to join people at the lowest level of righteousness.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : فيه بحث فإن يوسف من أكابر الأنبياء والصلاح أول درجات المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that objection: righteousness is a comprehensive, exalted station at every spiritual degree, not merely an initial rank; prophets, truthful ones, and martyrs remain righteous under their dominant titles.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا معنى ساقط ذهول عن حقيقة الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, dying Muslim signifies annihilation in God and joining the righteous signifies abiding through God, with the self effaced and sustained by eternal subsistence.
rows.anchor: فالتوفى مسلما إشارة إلى مرتبة الفناء في الله ، والإلحاق بالصالحين إشارة إلى مرتبة البقاء بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph told Zuleikha the dream and recited this prayer; she realized reunion would be followed by separation and wept.
rows.anchor: روى أن يوسف عليه السلام قص رؤياه المذكورة كما نقل عن الكاشفي على زليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Joseph is unseen news revealed through Gabriel; Muhammad was not present when his brothers plotted against him, which exposes the charge of revelation's deniers as implausible.
rows.anchor: المذكور من نبأ يوسف يا محمد من أنباء الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh and a group of Jews asked Muhammad about Joseph as a challenge; although his answer agreed with the Torah, they still did not believe and God consoled him.
rows.anchor: روي أن كفار قريش وجماعة من اليهود سألوا رسول الله عن قصة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the Prophet ardently showed people signs, most would not believe because their eternal dispositions are fixed; the command distinguishes those with potential so their felicity or misery becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: والحرص طلب شيء باجتهاد في إصابته بمؤمنين لعنادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that disbelievers outnumber believers because the purpose is the manifestation of the Perfect Human, who is one like a thousand.
rows.anchor: قلت : المقصود ظهور الإنسان الكامل وهو واحد كألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad seeks no payment for delivering the revelation and guidance, unlike professional transmitters of stories; the Qur'an is admonition and warning for all people, calling them to salvation.
rows.anchor: على الإنباء والإرشاد بالقرآن من أجر مال يعطونك كما يفعله حملة الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward lesson is that preaching, guidance, and good deeds should seek no benefit from people and should not be mixed with worldly or otherworldly rewards.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الدعوة والإرشاد وسائر أفعال الخير لا يطلب فيها المنفعة من الناس

rows.speaker: المثنوى
rows.claim: The Masnavi says a lover's joy and grief are God, and God Himself is the reward for service.
rows.anchor:
وفي المثنوى :
عاشقا نرا شادماني وغم اوست

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says the divine nature does not need the human nature, though it may call it to completion; it is complete in itself and completes others.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية يشير إلى أن اللاهوتية غير محتاجة إلى الناسوتية

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami explains the grammar of “ka-ayyin”: the comparative kāf joined ay loses the individual meanings and becomes an indeclinable expression of abundance, written with a final nūn.
rows.anchor: وكأين قال المولى الجامي في شرح الكافية من الكناية كأين وإنما بني لان كاف التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many signs of the Creator include the sun, moon, stars, rain, trees, animals, seas, and rivers; people see them but turn away without reflection, while the Qur'an makes their meaning clear.
rows.anchor: صفة آية كالشمس والقمر والنجوم والمطر والشجر والدواب والبحار والأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who reads the Qur'an while refusing its moral character is addressed as estranged from God and called to repent.
rows.anchor: والقرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات فمن لم يكن متصفا بأخلاقه إذا قرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may affirm God as creator while associating partners with Him in worship: the Meccans, idolaters, Jews, Christians, and Arab pilgrimage formula each express a different form of shirk.
rows.anchor: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون حيث يثبت له شريكا في المعبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary illustrates this with the Arab formula that names a partner owned by God, Meccans who call angels His daughters, idolaters who assign worship to idols, Jews who call Ezra God's son, and Christians who call Christ His son.
rows.anchor: تقول العرب في تلبيتهم : لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريكا هو لك
